 A lasting ‘rein’: West Carmel’s equestrian legacy gallops on 
 0 
 By 
 Piper Bailey 
 on 
 October 27, 2026 
 Carmel Cover Stories 
 Before neighborhoods and busy roads filled parts of west Carmel, horse farms and open pastures were a familiar sight.  
 For longtime residents Michelle Arnold and Jeannie Benz, horses were part of the landscape of their childhoods. Although development has changed the city around them, both have maintained a connection to the equestrian community. 
 “The west side of Carmel was horse barns and pastures filled with horses,” Benz said. “It was just synonymous with west Carmel.” 
 Arnold and Benz graduated from Carmel High School in 1990. They remember a time when riders could travel horseback through areas that have since been developed. Arnold recalled riding with friends through what is now the Bridgewater area, continuing toward Cool Creek Park and even stopping at McDonald’s. 
 “Nowadays, it’s too busy, you know? That whole area is so built up, and it’s just too busy with cars,” Arnold said. “You wouldn’t want to ride on the roads, which is sad because it was a lot of fun.” 
 Her passion for horses began as a child. She can’t remember a time when she “didn’t talk about horses, love horses, or want (her) own horse.” 
 After studying biology and secondary education,  she taught English riding and was an equestrian team coach at the University of Findlay in Ohio for 13 years. She returned to Carmel in 2014 and was a trainer at Treesdale Farms before opening Talbot Street Farm in June 2016. 
 “My dream upon dreams was to have my own horse training business, and I can honestly say that I am living my childhood dream,” Arnold said. “This is always what I’ve wanted to do.” 
 Talbot Street Farm, at 9919 Towne Rd., has 26 stalls and provides lessons for riders of different ages and experience levels. Arnold teaches lessons in hunter, jumpers and equitation disciplines. 
 Besides training, Arnold said the farm has become a community where riders form friendships across generations and support one another through life’s challenges. 
 “It really becomes a big family,” Arnold said. “It’s Talbot Street family, not just Talbot Street Farm. We’re a family.” 
 That community has welcomed Benz and her 15-year-old daughter, Ingrid. After attending a rodeo with her family, Benz rediscovered her love of horses. She arranged riding lessons for Ingrid, and secretly began taking lessons for herself.  
 They found their way to Talbot Street Farm, where both connected with Arnold and the horses. Ingrid rides Junior, while Benz rides Wyatt, a horse they can share despite their different experience levels. 
 For Ingrid, the appeal is simple. 
 “I just love them,” she said. “I think they’re sweet.” 
 She also enjoys jumping and building relationships with horses. For Benz, riding has offered an opportunity to develop confidence. 
 “There is such a trust that needs to be built up, because, as an adult coming into it, it’s quite terrifying,” she said. “I had to learn not only to trust myself, but to trust an animal.” 
 Equestrian photographer Luke VanDeWalle, who has photographed riders in Carmel, Zionsville and Westfield, has seen how those relationships extend beyond individual lessons. He said suburban growth has not erased the region’s rural roots. Stables provide opportunities for people to keep horses in their lives, whether they own an animal, lease one or take lessons. 
 VanDeWalle photographed the Benzes with their horses, capturing their shared experience of learning to ride alongside each other. 
 As Carmel continues to grow, places such as Talbot Street Farm offer a way for residents to maintain a tradition that once shaped much of the city’s landscape. The roads and surroundings may have changed, but for local riders, the connection to horses remains. 
 Jeannie and Ingrid Benz take horse riding lessons at Talbot Street Farm, 9919 Towne Rd. 
 Talbot Street Farm 
 Owner and head trainer : Michelle Arnold 
 Opened : June 2016 
 Location : 9919 Towne Rd. in Carmel 
 Capacity : 26 stalls — Currently at maximum capacity 
 Programs : Lessons for hunters, jumpers and in equitation 
 Facility features : Indoor and outdoor riding arenas and turnout paddocks 
 Learn more: Visit Talbot Street Farm on Facebook
